In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the new chemistry described here provides a viable and straightforward approach for the growth of Ge films that exhibit very high carrier concentrations and excellent device performance.
the chemistry approach presented here represents a viable route for achieving device-quality, high carrier concentration, n-doped Ge.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the inorganic hydride precursors As(SiH)3 and AsGeH3)3 provide an excellent platform for achieving high carrier concentrations and low resistivity in Ge films.
As(SiH2)2H and As(Ge)H2 are the most efficient precursors to dope germanium at very high levels.
the As-doped Ge n-layers grown using As(Si(H)3)3 and Ge3H8 have the highest carrier concentration among all Ge n-layers reported so far.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the inorganic hydride approach to low-temperature doping of Ge is highly versatile, enabling the fabrication of a wide variety of devices with high-performance properties that are on par with the best results reported in the literature.
As-doping of germanium using As(SiGeH3)3 precursors is a promising approach for the development of high performance optoelectronics and electronics.
